text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Productivity and Standards Board (PSB) says efforts pay off as not only training one in every three workers but also reaching those in problem groups.
- Employer, victim, forgive secretary who stole credit card.
- Singapore's Changi voted world's top airport by long-haul airline passengers.
- Goldsmith forgives employee who helped set up robbery of his shop.

- MCL Land, formerly Malayan Credit, tops bids for two sites in Urban Redevelopment Authority public tender of three residential land parcels, with overall response to auction viewed as "fair" and "expected" by analysts.
- Raffles Medical Group initial public offer shares subscribed 50 times.

- Bank Negara's new lending guidelines for purchases on properties may affect mega commercial projects in Kuala Lumpur including corporate player Tan Sri Vincent Tan's multibillion-dollar Linear City project.
- Australia lifts ban on foreigners owning local banks, paving way for Asian banks to seek significant presence in country.

- Listed Thai finance company Sri Dhana Finance and Securities in discussions of possible merger with Singapore's DBS Bank following measures by Thai central bank to spur consolidation among country's 91 finance companies.
- Yeo Ning Hong, former cabinet minister, leaves Singapore Technologies Pte Ltd to focus full-time on Port of Singapore Authority, of which he is chairman.
- Sinochem, China's premier state-owned trading conglomerate, puts off listing plan on the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
- Serial Systems investors who sold their shares enjoy at best a 3.5 cent or 5 percent premium in first two hours trading on Wednesday.
- Camerlin's deal to sell its Brierley Investment stake to Malaysia-listed Malex Industries should make a multi-million dollar paper profit for the company.
